children: Advanced Micro Devices
shares are on track to snap six straight sessions of gains, as the stock declined over 1% on Wednesday in afternoon trading.
Wall Street’s major averages traded lower Wednesday, with tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (
) falling over 1%, even as President Donald Trump raised the prospect of a negotiated end to the U.S. conflict with Iran.
The U.S. chipmaker gained about 24% in the preceding six sessions. Overall, the stock rose over 180% so far this year, compared to the 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

AMD is up nearly 35% over the past one month. The stock closed 1.3% higher on Tuesday at $623.77. September has been a favourable month for the stock, with 10 sessions trading in the green and just five closing in red.
Analysts are, however, very positive on the Lisa Su-led company.

Earlier on Monday, AMD surpassed a $1T market capitalization for the first time, helped by a broader rally in chip and AI companies, and became the latest chipmaker to reach the milestone, following Nvidia
, Broadcom
and Micron
. The stock closed about 10% higher on Monday.
Looking at Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating, AMD has a
with a score of 4.99 out of 5. The company received an A+ in the prospect of profitability and momentum, while it got a C+ in the valuation factor.
Turning to the
community, 44 analysts gave AMD a Buy or above, 11 analysts have given the stock a Hold recommendation, and no one recommended Sell or lower. Seeking Alpha analysts are also
and see the stock as a Buy.

“AMD is still showing a lot of long-term upside as the market continues to compound and AMD’s share within as well. I’m seeing nearly $350 billion in revenues by 2035 if this keeps up and AMD manages to capture 15% of the data center GPU market. The company is on the rise again, and I’ll be issuing another Strong Buy with this revised outlook for the business,” said Seeking Alpha analyst Andres Veurink.
Nvidia (
) shares also dropped on Wednesday after ending in the green for six straight sessions.
